transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-05-20
- Start: 16:00 PDT
- Duration approx 45m
- Attendees: Alex Park (Redwood AE), Samira Khan (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (NovaHealth CTO), Priya Rao (Head of ML), Mark Chen (DevOps), Aisha Gomez (Product)

Auto Summary:
Alex: quick agenda, parity mapping, demo the Redwood API, show Console and Optimize, then q&a and next steps.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i'm alex from redwood, with samira on the se side. how's it going?
[00:05] Jordan: good thanks, jordan here. excited to see the migration story, we've got prod traffic running on openai and a few Anthropic models and some Together endpoints for internal tools.
[00:12] Samira: great, we're gonna focus on mapping your existing calls—chat vs completion, embeddings, function calling—over to the Redwood API and show parity for things like streaming and stop tokens. also demo console and optimize tips.
[00:22] Priya: quick ask, we've got models run as both openai chat-completions and anthropic text-labs, and Together for some lower-cost encoding. main concerns: latency for conversational agents, cost, and keeping the same tokenization/embeddings outputs for search.
[00:35] Alex: totally, makes sense. Mark, any infra constraints? vpc, private deploy?
[00:39] Mark: ideally v-p-c and KMS, our security folks want audit logs and sso. we can't send full pii in the beginning but sample payloads are ok.
[00:45] Samira: noted. Redwood supports VPC/private, KMS/HSM integrations, SOC2, and audit logging — we'll share the security pack. also you can run private deployment if you need on-prem.
[00:55] Alex: ok quick mapping slide — so openai chat.messages -> Redwood chat endpoint is 1:1, message roles map, system/user/assistant the same. anthro's assistant/model naming might be slightly different but we have compatibility layers.
[01:12] Jordan: what about function calling? we use functions heavily.
[01:15] Samira: function calling is supported. small note: Together’s calling pattern was a little different for signature. we'll show how to map the schemas; Redwood accepts function definitions in the same JSON schema and returns a function call object you can execute. streaming also supported using chunked transfer.
[01:30] Alex: right, parity for temperature/top_p, max_tokens, stop sequences — all available. where things diverge is default tokenization differences between models — if you swap model families you'll need to re-eval a few prompts. we include quantization profiles and tokenization notes in the parity sheet.
[01:48] Priya: embeddings — we use openai text-embedding-3-small. want to keep vector stability. how do you handle model variants?
[01:55] Samira: Redwood has a model catalog with verified performance profiles; we can pin a model version. for exact parity we'd recommend running a side-by-side eval with your sample corpus. Optimize can suggest which quantized variant keeps cosine similarity within your delta.
[02:10] Alex: demo time — i'm going to share my screen, show a couple of curl examples, then console. bear with me while i switch windows.
[02:22] [screen share noise; small pause]
[02:30] Alex: ok here's a simple mapping: OpenAI call — POST /v1/chat/completions with messages array; Redwood call — POST /v1/responses or /v1/chat depending on SDK, but we have compatibility endpoints. example snippet... (reads code) 
[02:50] Alex: "curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"rw-chat-1","input":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a medical assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"..."}]}'"
[03:05] Jordan: so if i swap to rw-chat-1 will the tokens and answers be near identical to our current openai gpt-4 responses?
[03:12] Samira: closest is model selection — we list compatibility notes; you may see slight variations. for classification or deterministic outputs we recommend temperature=0 and also pinned model versions; for conversational fuzzier generation it's normal to see differences.
[03:26] Priya: do you provide rolling model rollouts? can we A/B test?
[03:30] Alex: yes, console supports canary and A/B routes, you can pin by route, and fallback policy if the primary model hits capacity.
[03:38] Mark: curious about latency — we have a 200ms p95 requirement for short prompts for chat. can Redwood meet that on hosted?
[03:46] Samira: depends on model size. for small-medium models and with KV caching and batching we can hit 150-250ms p95 in many regions. Dedicated gives more predictable SLAs — we can run benchmarks with your payload. we'll include a baseline run in the POC.
[03:59] Alex: talking cost, Optimize will recommend quantized variants and batching parameters. e.g., per-token cost on small quantized models vs large dense is often 3-4x difference.
[04:10] Jordan: any gotchas on prompt tokens or stop tokens? we use stop tokens a lot.
[04:14] Samira: stop tokens behave the same; streaming and partial tokens are supported. occasionally transcription and stop behaviour vary per model; that's why we do the eval.
[04:25] Aisha: console UI looks neat — can you show traces for a specific request path?
[04:29] Alex: sure. switching to Console view — here is per-route analytics, token-level cost breakdown, traces with latency waterfall, and prompt diffs. you can set alerts on regressions tied to your evaluation prompt sets.
[04:45] [brief pause while Alex flips to a demo dashboard] 
[04:55] Alex: also Optimize tab here suggests batching window sizes, cache TTLs for prefix caching, and recommended quant profiles. we can auto-suggest retention policies to save cost.
[05:10] Priya: what about embeddings versioning — we need stable vectors for semantic search, not just similar ones.
[05:15] Samira: two approaches: 1) pin to a specific model and quantization, run an alignment job to measure cosine drift; 2) if you need exact bit-level identity that's usually not possible across different model vendors; but for product search you only need cosine similarity within a tolerance, and we can help set thresholds in Optimize.
[05:33] Jordan: security checklist — SOC2, SSO, RBAC, KMS, audit logs, region residency. do you have that?
[05:40] Alex: yes SOC2 Type II, SAML SSO, RBAC in console, KMS for encryption, audit logs available via console and export. for region residency we offer private deployment and VPC options for enterprise. we'll attach the security pack.
[05:53] Mark: for POC, we'd want a VPC workspace or Dedicated trial and the ability to route traffic from our infra. network egress rules and a list of IPs?
[06:01] Samira: we'll share network checklist including IP ranges and port requirements. for Dedicated we'll run through the architecture diagram.
[06:10] Alex: quick note on private deployment — it can be customer-controlled control plane or full on-prem package; depends on compliance.
[06:18] Priya: latency and consistent outputs are key — also we'd like to test function calling firm against our orchestrator.
[06:25] Samira: totally. show of hands — do we want to include Together models mapping?
[06:28] Jordan: yes, we use Together for cheaper embedding runs.
[06:31] Samira: ok mapping note: Together's api param names are slightly different but semantics match; we provide adapter snippets in the parity sheet.
[06:40] Alex: i'm going to walk through a quick parity spreadsheet example — openai param -> redwood param, anthro param -> redwood param, together param -> redwood param, plus notes on tokenization and embedding differences.
[06:50] [Alex pastes a short table into chat]
[06:54] Alex: example: openai "model": "gpt-4o" -> redwood "model": "rw-chat-1"; openai "messages" -> redwood "input" array; openai function calling "functions" -> same name; streaming uses SSE/chunked.
[07:10] Priya: how about SDK language parity? we use node/python.
[07:14] Samira: we have official SDKs in python, node, and go — code snippets will look basically the same. we also provide a quickstart repo so you can swap endpoints and keys.
[07:24] Mark: in terms of throttling and rate limits, how do you handle burst traffic?
[07:28] Alex: Hosted has rate limits by plan, but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and autoscale policies. we also support burst capacity for spiky traffic. you can configure routing policies for region/cost tier fallbacks.
[07:40] Jordan: what's the onboarding timeline for a POC?
[07:44] Samira: usually 2-4 weeks from sample data to run benchmarks and integration tests — baseline runs within the first week, then a 2-week performance and quality window. for Dedicated or Private it can be longer depending on procurement.
[07:56] Alex: okay let's demo a function call mapping quickly — i'll show a chat -> function call -> app flow using streaming.
[08:03] [demo noise: live code shown]
[08:20] Alex: here the function schema is returned as call: { name: "get_medical_record", arguments: "{...}" } you then execute your function and pass the result back. it's the same pattern you use today.
[08:32] Priya: good. how do you handle logging of responses that include PHI?
[08:36] Samira: Redwood can disable response retention at the workspace level, or redact fields via a webhook; in private deployments you keep full control. KMS ensures keys are customer-managed if needed.
[08:48] Aisha: any guidance for cost optimization for search-heavy apps?
[08:52] Alex: yes, Optimize will recommend embedding batching, quantized embedding models, caching top-k search results, and setting TTLs. for high QPS search we often recommend smaller embedding dims with retraining of the reranker if needed.
[09:06] Jordan: ok, can we get an estimate for cost comparing our current stack? we pay per token on openai and per-embedding on Together.
[09:12] Alex: we'll prepare a cost delta using your traffic profile — needs traffic histogram and prompt size distribution. that's in the next steps.
[09:20] [sound of typing]
[09:28] Mark: what's the PII handling for logs in hosted mode?
[09:31] Samira: by default we store logs for X days; for enterprise you can opt-out of storage or set custom retention and redaction. details in the security pack.
[09:40] Priya: any automated eval tooling? we run prompt sets nightly for regressions.
[09:44] Alex: yes, built-in evals let you run prompt sets and surface regressions with diffs and metric drops; you can link alerts to a regression threshold.
[09:54] Jordan: excellent. let's recap and next steps.
[09:58] Alex: recap — we'll send parity mapping sheet, security pack, and a quickstart repo. Samira will run baseline latency runs if you provide sample prompts and a small dataset. schedule POC kickoff week of june 1.
[10:12] Priya: i can share sample prompts by monday. Mark will start network checklist.
[10:18] Alex: perfect — action items we'll follow up in email. thanks everyone.
[10:22] Jordan: thanks, appreciate it.
[10:25] [meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hears (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, "Reedwood" instead of Redwood), filler words and overlaps preserved.
